media:group.media:title: Magnet technology: Advancing fusion research
media:group.media:description:
Today, superconducting magnets are essential to both high energy physics and fusion energy research.
Certain materials, when cooled to extreme temperatures, lose all electrical resistance and can carry extraordinary currents, making them capable of generating magnetic fields far beyond what conventional electromagnets can achieve.
The MAGNES test bed at Fermilab will provide access to a volume of high magnetic field that can be used for testing the superconducting cables that would go into such a reactor. And at the heart of MAGNES will be a powerful magnet designed and fabricated by @berkeleylab.
The facility’s research will directly inform the design of magnets for next-generation fusion devices.
Learn more at https://news.fnal.gov/2026/10/physics-and-fusion-research-advances-through-fermilabs-magnes/

media:group.media:title: Why we need quantum computers
media:group.media:description:
A classical computer solves problems one step at a time. But a quantum computer can explore multiple possibilities simultaneously.
In the future, quantum computers could solve advanced physics questions and bring breakthroughs in medicine and national security.
That's the power of quantum computing. 💪
The catch?
Today, qubits are fragile, lasting mere milliseconds in a quantum state before environmental interference collapses them. Fermilab physicists are working to extend this coherence time.
#FermilabTech #Fermilab #Quantum #QuantumPhysics #Technology #QuantumScience

media:group.media:title: What is a quantum sensor?
media:group.media:description:
Unlocking the secrets of the universe with quantum science 🌌
Quantum sensors are used to explore some of the most fundamental questions in physics including hunting for dark matter.
Fermilab's QUIET lab sits 100 meters underground to allow scientists to study the performance of qubits protected from cosmic radiation. Together with its above-ground counterpart, the LOUD lab, QUIET enables controlled experiments to develop quantum sensors for dark matter detection and quantum computing.
Join Fermilab scientists Rakshya Khatiwada and Daniel Baxter as they break down what quantum sensors are, how they work, and why they can make measurements traditional sensors can’t.
#QuantumSensors #QuantumScience #Fermilab #QUIETLab #QuantumComputing #DarkMatter #ParticlePhysics #FermilabTech

entry.title: PIP-II | Installing the first gear of the new linac

media:group.media:title: PIP-II | Installing the first gear of the new linac
media:group.media:description:
From past breakthroughs to future frontiers! ✨ 70 years after the first neutrino detection, we're laying the groundwork for tomorrow's cosmic discoveries.
Recently, the first piece of our new linear accelerator’s beamline was moved into the accelerator tunnel! This radio-frequency quadrupole — designed and built by our partners at Berkeley Lab — will serve as the "first gear" of the upgraded Fermilab accelerator complex.
The Proton Improvement Plan II, or PIP-II, is an essential enhancement to the Fermilab Accelerator Complex, powering the world’s most intense neutrino beam for the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment.

media:group.media:title: Genesis Mission | Accelerating Discovery
media:group.media:description:
We’re proud to help drive the #GenesisMission. With the U.S. Department of Energy, we are using AI to accelerate discovery and transform the scientific process.
Fermilab is a world-recognized leader in particle accelerator science and technology. Our accelerators send powerful particle beams traveling at nearly the speed of light across miles of beamlines, enabling physics experiments that generate massive streams of data for scientific discovery.
With our world’s largest datasets, and complex detector and accelerator systems, the lab’s high-energy research creates unique opportunities for AI innovations. Researchers at Fermilab develop and implement AI tools to improve measurements, optimize operations and accelerate discovery.
Learn more at https://artificialintelligence.fnal.gov
#AI #Fermilab #physics #NationalAIDay

media:group.media:title: #Neutrino70 | Chasing cosmic relics
media:group.media:description:
Why are we here? 🌌
It’s one of humanity’s oldest questions, and the answer might be written in ghostly particles called neutrinos.
These "cosmic relics" have been bouncing around the universe since the dawn of time, carrying secrets from the hearts of supernovae and the birth of the cosmos.
At Fermilab, we don't just wait to catch them. We use our powerful accelerator complex to actually create, control, and study our own neutrino beams, helping us solve the biggest mysteries left in physics.
#Neutrino70 #Fermilab #ParticlePhysics #Cosmology #DUNEscience
